Parco Bosco in Città — Milan, Italy

Relatively safer day Average night

In detail

A well-loved urban forest park in the San Siro area, popular with families and cyclists, and explicitly named among the five safest zones in Milan by a 2025 crime-index ranking. A genuinely pleasant, low-crime green space by day. The usual big-city-park caveat still applies at night: wooded, unlit areas away from the main paths are best avoided when walking alone after dark, even in a generally safe neighbourhood.

Frequently asked questions

Is Parco Bosco in Città safe?

Wandroz currently rates Parco Bosco in Città in Milan as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Milan during the day and roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Milan at night. This comes from a structured local-source assessment: an area-level review of credible local sources — local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist — consolidated across sources rather than taken from a single report. Milan publishes no comparable neighbourhood-level crime dataset; where a city does, Wandroz uses it instead.

Is Parco Bosco in Città safe at night?

At night, Parco Bosco in Città is rated as roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Milan. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Parco Bosco in Città a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Parco Bosco in Città's day rating (relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Milan) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late.
